tei:bibl.tei:title: אֵימָתַי נִגְלָה לַנֶּאֱהָב
Eimatai Niglah la-Ne'ehav — an original 'Aqedah piyyuṭ by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer
tei:bibl.tei:author: Isaac Gantwerk Mayer
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: ‘Aqedah piyyuṭim are generally, in Ashkenazi seliḥot cycles, the second-to-last seliḥah, preceding the pizmon. Traditionally written in rhyming quatrains, they retell the narrative of the binding of Isaac. There are dozens of ‘aqedah piyyutim, but almost all of them focus on the perspective of Abraham. This is unsurprising, since Abraham’s perspective is largely the focus in the midrash. But it always felt like a bit of a lost opportunity to me. I’ve always sympathized more with Isaac’s perspective, perhaps for obvious reasons (my Hebrew name is יצחק הראל בן אברהם הכהן Isaac Mountain-of-God son of Abraham, the Person-who-sacrifices, after all). And the question of when did Isaac realize what was happening, and how did he react to it, is a fascinating and disturbing one to me. This ‘aqedah is meant to reflect that question. Directed at Isaac, it asks him: when did you know, and how did you respond when you did? And will you remember us before God?
